summary: Same 1D red-fire idea and near-identical spatial profile shape (corr 0.96-0.98 on non-clipping rigs), but the port misses the original's defining long-period behaviour — the original alternates ~55 s of animation with a 32.77 s byte-identical FREEZE (37-47% of runtime depending on fps) and the port never freezes at all — and on top of that the port advects ~1.9x too fast at the default 20 fps (time-based vs the original's frame-stepped ~1.1 px/frame) and settles ~45% dimmer, ~35% shorter and much redder.
observations: Neither side exposes any settable control (--probe-controls: 'no settable controls' on both orig and port). Control surfaces match; dials: [].
Both sides compile and run with no compile/runtime errors, both report wantsSensors:false, both start near-black and light up within the first second.

FREEZE CYCLES (the headline). The original periodically stops dead: every rendered pixel is byte-identical for 32.77-32.80 s, then animation resumes. Measured at 5 fps over 400 s the freezes are 36.2-69.0, 105.4-138.2, 174.6-207.4, 243.8-276.6, 313.0-345.8, 382.2-400.0 s — duration exactly 32.8 s each, period exactly 69.2 s, 45.5% of all frames frozen. At 20 fps over 150 s: freeze 54.55-87.35 s (32.80 s) and next onset 141.90 s, i.e. period 87.35 s, 37.5% frozen (819/3000 zero-motion frames). At 2 fps over 240 s: onsets 34.0 / 101.0 / 167.5 s, duration 32.5-33.0 s, period 66.75 s. The freeze DURATION is fps-invariant at 32.768 s; the active stretch between freezes is fps-dependent (34 s at 2 fps, 36.4 s at 5 fps, 54.55 s at 20 fps).

Freeze verified as a true hold, not a dim/slow false-read: a --dump inside the freeze (skip 60, times 60 / 60.05 / 61 / 65 / 70 / 79 s) returns SIX byte-identical original frames, at mean brightness 95 (not dark) — the fire is stuck as a bright still image mid-flame. The port's dumps at the same six times are all different from each other.

The port NEVER freezes: 1 zero-motion frame out of 3000 at 20 fps/150 s, 1/2000 at 5 fps/400 s, 1/480 at 2 fps/240 s, 1-2/2000 at seeds 7 and 1234 — in every case only the unavoidable first captured frame.
The freeze is deterministic, not RNG: at seeds 1, 7 and 1234 the original's 20 fps freeze lands at exactly 54.55-87.35 s every time. The port stays freeze-free at all three seeds.

WARM-UP. The original ramps: mean brightness in 2 s bins at 20 fps runs 22, 71, 72, 57, 74, 90, 98, 103 ... and then hovers 90-125 for the rest of a 150 s run. The port has no ramp — its 2 s bins hover 40-70 from t=0 to t=150 s. The two sides therefore agree over a short window and diverge after ~6 s: the 6 s/20 fps baseline is orig mean 55 / port 54 (meanR 116 vs 119, meanG 42 vs 39, motion 12.2 vs 12.4), while 150 s at 20 fps is orig 96 / port 55.

SETTLED BRIGHTNESS (20 fps, 60 px, active regimes only): orig 99.9 (t=10-30 s), 107.1 (t=30-54.5 s), 94.7 (t=87-110 s), 100.0 (t=110-141 s); port 52.7 / 54.6 / 61.5 / 52.0 over the same windows. Same ~2x gap at seed 7 (orig 95-131 vs port 55-59) and seed 1234 (orig 91-107 vs port 57-62).

SETTLED COLOUR (same windows): orig meanR ~193-203, meanG ~83-100, meanB ~15-18; port meanR ~117-134, meanG ~34-46, meanB ~3. The port's green channel is roughly 2.4x low and its blue roughly 5x low — it reads as a red fire with a small yellow tip, the original as a yellow-cored fire with red edges.

FLAME LENGTH on the default 60 px rig (mean of 40 dumps over t=30-49.5 s, 20 fps): luminance half-max at pixel 30 (orig) vs pixel 19 (port); lum at px 40 = 71.6 vs 16.1, at px 50 = 35.0 vs 1.5, at px 59 = 13.8 vs 0.0. The original keeps the far end faintly ember-lit ([57,0,0] at px 58); the port is fully black past ~px 46. Last index with meanG >= 100: orig 27, port 11; with meanG >= 20: orig 39, port 24.

RIG SWEEP shows the same law with a scale offset, not a different model. Feature size is absolute (a fixed ~50-60 px flame regardless of strip length), on BOTH sides. At 150 px (skip 30, 20 s, 40 dumps): orig peakLum 120.9 / half-max @24 / last-lit @62 / meanR 41.7 / meanG 11.6; port peakLum 98.2 / half-max @19 / last-lit @50 / meanR 31.2 / meanG 8.2; profile correlation 0.980. At 300 px: orig peakLum 75.4 / half-max @27 / last-lit @63 / meanG 3.4; port 43.9 / @28 / @46 / meanG 1.1; correlation 0.958. At 12 px both rail across the whole strip (orig peak 253, port 241). So the shape of the heat profile is right; its amplitude is ~30-45% low everywhere and its tail ~20% short.

Clipping caveat: on the default 60 px rig the original's red channel is railed at 255 across roughly pixels 0-32 in its settled regime while the port is not, so the 60 px numbers overstate the gap. The 150/300 px runs (railedR 8.9%/2.7% orig, 6.3%/1.1% port) are the clean comparison and still show the port 30-45% dim.

MOTION RATE / FRAME COUPLING. Template-matching pixels 8-44 between --dump frames 0.1 s apart at t=30 s: original 14.0 px/s at 10 fps, 21.5 px/s at 20 fps, 45.5 px/s at 40 fps (i.e. 1.40 / 1.07 / 1.14 px per FRAME) — frame-stepped. Port 41.0 / 41.0 / ~40.6 px/s at the same three rates (4.10 / 2.05 / 0.74 px per frame) — time-based and fps-invariant. At the harness default 20 fps the port advects ~1.9x too fast; the two rates coincide near 38-40 fps. Direction agrees on both sides (strictly rightward from pixel 0, no bounce or reversal).

The `motion` stat is misleading for this diagnosis, as in the previous judgement: whole-rig motion reads 8/10/11 for the original and 18/13/8 for the port across 10/20/40 fps, i.e. it suggests the OPPOSITE coupling. Only position tracking settles it.

TEXTURE. In matched settled windows (skip 30, 20 s, 20 fps waterfalls) the original's rightward trails are broad, overlapping, steeply-sloped slabs that keep most of the strip warm; the port's are thinner, shallower-sloped (faster), sparser individual ember trails with substantially more black between them and a hard edge around pixel 46. Same character visible at 6 s baseline, 60 s survey, 150 s and both alternate seeds.

Reference-behaviour note: per the 2026-08-29 oracle probing (plain add wraps at the 16.16 range ends on real Pixel Blaze hardware), the original's 32.768 s freezes are authentic hardware behaviour, not an engine artefact — a real PB running this pattern freezes identically. They are therefore scored as part of the pattern in this re-judge, reversing the previous verdict's decision to exclude them.
feedback: Reproduce the freeze cycles. This is the biggest single gap and the most visible one: the original runs, then holds a byte-identical still frame for 32.768 s, then runs again — 37% of its runtime at 20 fps, 45% at 5 fps. The port animates continuously forever (1 zero-motion frame in 3000). The freeze is deterministic (identical at seeds 1/7/1234), its duration is fps-invariant at 32.768 s, and its onset/period are not: active stretch 34 s at 2 fps, 36.4 s at 5 fps, 54.55 s at 20 fps. That signature (a fixed-point accumulator running into the 16.16 range end and wrapping) is what the port must reproduce, freeze phase and duration included, not just 'some pause'.

Slow the advection and match the original's frame coupling. Original: frame-stepped at ~1.1 px per rendered frame (14 px/s at 10 fps, 21.5 px/s at 20 fps, 45.5 px/s at 40 fps). Port: time-based at a constant ~41 px/s at every rate. At the default 20 fps the port is ~1.9x too fast. Matching the original means stepping per frame, not per second; a pure speed rescale to 21.5 px/s would fix 20 fps only and would still diverge at 10 and 40 fps.

Raise the heat. In the settled active regime the original sits at mean brightness ~95-107 on the 60 px rig versus the port's ~52-62. Measured where neither side clips: at 150 px orig peak luminance 120.9 vs port 98.2 and mean R 41.7 vs 31.2; at 300 px 75.4 vs 43.9 and 14.5 vs 9.4. Target roughly +40-70% on peak/mean heat.

Add the warm-up. The original starts cool (mean brightness ~22 in the first 2 s) and climbs to its ~100 plateau over about 10-14 s at 20 fps; the port is flat at ~40-70 from the first frame. The port's steady state is essentially the original's first five seconds, held forever.

Add yellow and white through the mid-strip. Settled meanG should be ~85-100, not ~34-46, and meanB ~15-18, not ~3. Concretely on the 60 px rig the last pixel with mean G >= 100 should be around index 27 (port: 11) and with mean G >= 20 around index 39 (port: 24). Right now the fire is red with a small yellow tip instead of yellow-cored with red edges.

Extend the tail. Luminance half-max should land near pixel 30 of 60 (port: 19), and the far end of the strip should stay faintly ember-lit (~[57,0,0] at pixel 58) instead of going hard black past pixel 46. Confirmed off-default too: at 150 px last-lit index 62 (orig) vs 50 (port); at 300 px 63 vs 46. The absolute-length law is already correct — only the tail's reach and amplitude are short.

Soften and thicken the ember texture: the original's rightward trails are broad overlapping slabs, the port's are thin sparse high-contrast streaks with a lot of black between them. More inter-pixel diffusion / longer-lived heat cells would close this. (Note the profile SHAPE already correlates 0.96-0.98 with the original at 150 and 300 px, so the model is close — this is an amplitude/diffusion tuning gap, not a structural rewrite.)

Do not tune against the default 60 px rig alone: the original's red channel rails at 255 across pixels 0-32 there, which distorts every profile and palette comparison. Verify fixes at --pixels 150 and --pixels 300 where neither side clips.
